causes.label: Controls improperly set.
remedies: To turn from the OFF position, push the knob in and then turn.
The knob can only be turned in a counterclockwise direction.
When the knob is at any other position, it can be turned in either direction without being pushed in.

causes.label: The fan control knob is improperly set.
remedies: Turn knob in clockwise direction to turn fan on.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 36: "The fan control knob is improperly set."

causes.label: Cord improperly connected or power turned off.
remedies: Check connections.
Turn on power at the fuse box.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 36: "Cord improperly connected or power turned off."

causes.label: Clogged filter.
remedies: Clean filter per instructions.

causes.label: House too airtight.
remedies: Open a window slightly to provide fresh air source.

causes.label: Wall cap obstructed.
remedies: Remove blockage from exterior wall cap.

causes.label: Wall cap damper door stuck.
remedies: Check exterior wall cap damper door for free movement or obstruction.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 36: "Wall cap damper door stuck."

causes.label: Duct length exceeds recommended 100 equivalent foot maximum.
remedies: Reduce number of elbows to simplify duct run.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 36: "Duct length exceeds recommended 100 equivalent foot maximum."

symptoms.symptom: Areas of discoloration or dark streaks on the cooktop

causes.label: Improper cookware being used.
remedies: Marks from aluminum and copper pans as well as mineral deposits from water or food can be removed with the cleaning cream.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 36: "Improper cookware being used."

causes.label: Hot surface on a model with a lightcolored cooktop.
remedies: This is normal.
The surface may appear discolored when it is hot.
This is temporary and will disappear as the glass cools.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 36: "Hot surface on a model with a lightcolored cooktop."

causes.label: Incorrect cleaning methods being used.
